text: The Burrows-Wheeler transform, which enables fast and memory-efficient short-read alignment, is the algorithmic basis of which widely used aligners?
explanation: The chapter states directly that the Burrows-Wheeler transform is the basis of BWA and bowtie2 alignment, which use it (via the FM-index) for compressed, fast substring search against a reference genome. BLAST/DIAMOND instead rely on seed-and-extend heuristics with different indexing schemes, and GATK/Picard are variant-calling and BAM-processing toolkits rather than BWT-based aligners; Needleman-Wunsch/Smith-Waterman are dynamic-programming alignment algorithms, not transform-based indexing methods.
